projects.content_zh: 禹王宫位于商洛市山阳县城东关，又名湖广会馆。1981年公布为山阳县重点文物保护单位，2003年公布为陕西省重点文物保护单位。据《建修湖广会馆引》载：明末清初，山阳由于屡遭战乱，人口大减，到清乾隆年间，政府积极推行移民政策，各省移民纷纷来山阳定居谋生，而湖广之人更多，遂于清乾隆五十七年（1792年）修建湖广会馆。因正殿主神塑大禹像，所以后湖广会馆取名禹王宫。禹王宫总建筑面积3000平方米，规模宏伟。其布局沿纵轴线，依次为牌楼门、戏楼、广场、前殿、后殿，前后大殿东西两侧各有两排六间偏殿。禹王宫建筑为砖砌墙面，屋面均为五脊硬山。檐山生起，瓦当项纵，檐下由93个鸟拱构成，挑柱之间有麒麟鹏鸟衔接，风格独特。屋面采用虎头兽瓦，脊上雕饰有飞龙戏凤、珍禽异兽、名花异卉等图案。檐下斗拱层层叠出，挑柱间的撑拱均属镂空木雕。梁枋的主要部位均饰木雕，雕刻手法洗练精妙，生动流畅。石柱础造型各异，石雕图案丰富多彩，雕刻手法洗练精妙，生动流畅。主殿宽敞，四周饰以人物故事等壁画，栩栩如生，具有很高的艺术价值。
projects.content_en: Yu the Great Palace is located in the east pass of Shanyang County town, Shangluo City, also called the Huguang Guild Hall. It was designated as a Key Cultural Heritage Site of Shanyang County in 1981 and a Shaanxi Provincial Key Cultural Heritage Site in 2003. According to the 'Preface to the Construction and Repair of the Huguang Guild Hall': at the end of the Ming and beginning of the Qing dynasties, Shanyang suffered repeated wars and chaos, with a greatly reduced population; by the Qianlong period of Qing, the government actively implemented immigration policies, and immigrants from various provinces came to Shanyang to settle and make a living, with more people from Huguang (Hubei and Hunan), so the Huguang Guild Hall was built in the 57th year of Qianlong, Qing (1792). Because the main deity statue in the main hall was of Yu the Great, the Huguang Guild Hall was later named Yu the Great Palace. Yu the Great Palace has a total building area of 3,000 square meters, with a magnificent scale. Its layout follows the longitudinal axis, sequentially including the archway gate, opera tower, square, front hall, and rear hall; on the east and west sides of the front and rear main halls, there are two rows of six side halls each. The buildings of Yu the Great Palace have brick walls, with five-ridge flush gable roofs. The eaves and gables have shengqi (rise), with tile caps and vertical ridges; under the eaves, 93 bird-shaped bracket sets (dougong) are formed, with qilin and peng birds connecting between the挑 columns, with a unique style. The roof uses tiger-head beast tiles, with the ridges carved and decorated with patterns such as flying dragons playing with phoenixes, rare birds and animals, and famous flowers and exotic plants. Under the eaves, the dougong stacks out layer by layer, and the supporting brackets between the挑 columns are all hollowed-out wood carvings. The main parts of the beams and枋 are all decorated with wood carvings, with refined and exquisite carving techniques, vivid and fluent. The stone column bases have various shapes, with rich and colorful stone carving patterns, with refined and exquisite carving techniques, vivid and fluent. The main hall is spacious, with murals such as character stories decorated on all four sides, lifelike, with high artistic value.

projects.content_zh: 黄帝陵是中华民族始祖黄帝轩辕氏的陵墓，因其地处陕西省黄陵县城北桥山之巅，故又称桥陵。黄帝陵自古即为中国历代帝王和著名人士祭祀黄帝的场所，素有天下第一陵之称。1961年公布为全国第一批重点文物保护单位。史载轩辕黄帝庙初建于汉代，由陵墓和轩辕黄帝庙两部分组成。唐代宗大历五年（公元770年）于桥山西麓置黄帝庙，并对轩辕黄帝庙进行历时两年的重修扩建，栽植柏树1140株。宋太祖开宝二年（公元969年），因桥山西麓的黄帝庙屡受沮河水侵袭，遂于桥山东麓今址移建黄帝庙。此后，元、明、清各代均对其进行维护、修建。民国二十八年（1939年），陕西省政府设立黄帝陵园管理处。1944年，建陵园祭祀亭，亭内竖蒋中正手书黄帝陵石碑。1992年起，国家、陕西省政府不间断地对黄帝陵进行大规模规划整修，通过祭祀大殿、周边环境整治等系列工程，形成了祭祀谒陵的完整建筑体系。黄帝陵墓封土高3.6米，周长48米。陵前有明嘉靖十五年（1536年）碑刻桥山龙驭，意为黄帝驭龙升天之处。封土前为一祭亭，歇山顶，飞檐起翘，气宇轩昂，亭内立有郭沫若手书黄帝陵碑石。陵区周围有红墙围护，东南侧设棂星门。陵前正南围墙外是土筑高台，即汉武仙台，传为汉武帝祭祀黄帝所筑。《史记·封禅书》载：汉武帝北巡朔方，勒兵十余万还祭黄帝冢桥山。此台高20余米，现已用块石砌筑并建有登台石阶、云板及护栏等。轩辕黄帝庙占地面积约十亩，平面呈方形。其主要建筑有山门、过厅和大殿等。山门面阔五间，单檐歇山顶，门上悬一匾，上书轩辕黄帝庙五个大字。山门之后为过厅三间，厅内保存有70余块明清石碑，大多为明清两代修建轩辕黄帝庙和祭祀黄帝情况实录。大殿面阔七间，单檐歇山顶，四周回廊，殿内供奉轩辕黄帝牌位。轩辕黄帝庙内古树遍布，其中尤以黄帝手植柏与汉武帝挂甲柏最为著名。黄帝手植柏高20余米，胸径11米，苍劲挺拔，冠盖蔽空。相传为轩辕黄帝亲手所植，距今5000多年，是世界上最古老的柏树。汉武帝挂甲柏又称将军柏，位于大殿前月台的西阶下，其体量比黄帝手植柏略小。据说汉武帝当年祭祀黄帝陵时，曾将自己身上的铠甲挂于树上。该树周身斑痕密布，纵横成行，柏液中出，似有断钉在内，枝干皆然。
projects.content_en: The Yellow Emperor Mausoleum is the mausoleum of Xuanyuan Shi, the Yellow Emperor, the ancestor of the Chinese nation. Because it is located at the top of Qiaoshan Mountain, north of Huangling County town, Shaanxi Province, it is also called Qiaoling. The Yellow Emperor Mausoleum has been a place for Chinese emperors and famous people of all dynasties to sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor since ancient times, known as 'the First Mausoleum Under Heaven.' It was designated as one of the first batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1961. According to historical records, the Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple was first built in the Han Dynasty, consisting of two parts: the mausoleum and the Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple. In the 5th year of Dali of Emperor Daizong of Tang (770 AD), the Yellow Emperor Temple was established at the western foot of Qiaoshan Mountain, and the Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple was rebuilt and expanded over two years, with 1,140 cypress trees planted. In the 2nd year of Kaibao of Emperor Taizu of Song (969 AD), because the Yellow Emperor Temple at the western foot of Qiaoshan Mountain was repeatedly invaded by the Ju River, it was moved to the current site at the eastern foot of Qiaoshan Mountain. Thereafter, the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties all maintained and constructed it. In the 28th year of the Republic (1939), the Shaanxi Provincial Government established the Yellow Emperor Mausoleum Management Office. In 1944, a mausoleum sacrificial pavilion was built, with a stone stele of 'Yellow Emperor Mausoleum' handwritten by Chiang Kai-shek erected inside. Since 1992, the state and the Shaanxi Provincial Government have continuously carried out large-scale planning and renovation of the Yellow Emperor Mausoleum, through a series of projects such as the sacrificial hall and surrounding environment renovation, forming a complete architectural system for sacrifice and mausoleum visits. The mound of the Yellow Emperor Mausoleum is 3.6 m high and 48 m in circumference. In front of the mausoleum, there is a stele carved in the 15th year of Jiajing, Ming (1536), inscribed 'Qiaoshan Longyu,' meaning the place where the Yellow Emperor rode a dragon to ascend to heaven. In front of the mound is a sacrificial pavilion, with a hip-and-gable roof, upturned flying eaves, and an imposing appearance; inside the pavilion stands a stone stele of 'Yellow Emperor Mausoleum' handwritten by Guo Moruo. The mausoleum area is surrounded by red walls, with a Lingxing Gate on the southeast side. Outside the south wall in front of the mausoleum is an earthen high platform, namely the Hanwu Immortal Platform, legendarily built by Emperor Wu of Han to sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor. The 'Records of the Grand Historian: Treatise on Feng and Shan Sacrifices' records: Emperor Wu of Han toured north to Shuofang, leading more than 100,000 troops, and returned to sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor's tomb at Qiaoshan. This platform is more than 20 m high, and has now been built with block stones, with stone steps for climbing, cloud boards, and guardrails. The Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple covers about ten mu, with a square plane. Its main buildings include the mountain gate, passage hall, and main hall. The mountain gate is five bays wide, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof; a plaque hangs on the gate, inscribed with the five large characters 'Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple.' Behind the mountain gate is a three-bay passage hall, in which more than 70 Ming-Qing stone steles are preserved, mostly records of the construction of the Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple and the sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor in the Ming and Qing dynasties. The main hall is seven bays wide, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof and surrounding corridors; inside the hall, the spirit tablet of Xuanyuan the Yellow Emperor is enshrined. Ancient trees are everywhere in the Xuanyuan Yellow Emperor Temple, among which the Yellow Emperor's Hand-Planted Cypress and Emperor Wu of Han's Armor-Hanging Cypress are the most famous. The Yellow Emperor's Hand-Planted Cypress is more than 20 m high, with a breast diameter of 11 m, vigorous and upright, with its crown covering the sky. Legend has it that it was planted by Xuanyuan the Yellow Emperor himself, more than 5,000 years ago, and is the oldest cypress tree in the world. Emperor Wu of Han's Armor-Hanging Cypress, also called the General Cypress, is located under the west steps of the moon platform in front of the main hall, with a slightly smaller size than the Yellow Emperor's Hand-Planted Cypress. It is said that when Emperor Wu of Han sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor Mausoleum, he hung his armor on the tree. This tree is covered with dense scars all over, in rows vertically and horizontally, with cypress sap oozing out, as if there were broken nails inside, and all branches are like this.

projects.content_zh: 秦人是商末战乱西迁的华夏族。在其崛起、昌盛、灭亡的漫长历史进程中，秦人先后营建了西垂、衙、平阳、雍、栎阳、咸阳、芷阳、杜东、韩森寨、骊山共十个陵区。这些建造实践，使秦代先民逐步积累了陵园、墓葬、封土、礼制建筑、陪葬墓、陪葬坑、门阙等陵墓营造经验，最终推动了从集中公墓到独立陵园的形制巨变，奠定了中国古代帝王陵墓制度的基础。秦公帝王陵园包括四大陵区，即天水陵区、雍城陵区、栎阳陵区和咸阳陵区。陵园建立顺序自西而东，即由天水附近的秦、西垂到关中的雍城、栎阳和咸阳，其设立符合秦公陵园建筑随国都而转移的总体规律。个别帝王因新迁都城未竟而归葬于原都城，如襄公、文公等虽已越过陇山，但仍归葬陇山以西的西垂陵区，灵公等虽从雍城迁往泾阳，但仍归葬雍城。雍城秦公陵园位于今宝鸡市凤翔县南源，总面积约21平方公里。整个陵区东西长约12公里，南北宽约3公里，总面积约36平方公里。陵区西、南、北三侧均发现有宽2至7米、深2至6米作为其防护屏障的围沟。各陵园背西面东，呈雁翎形排列，规模宏大。1988年公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位。雍城秦公陵园是目前所知最大的秦国国君陵寝之地。自秦穆公起当有多位秦国国君葬于此。陵园平面呈南北长、东西窄的长方形，具有防护设施。墓葬位于陵园南半部，东面为殉葬坑，这种布局形式也为后来秦始皇陵园所继承。雍城秦公陵园目前已钻探51座大墓，平面形制可分为丰字形、中字形、甲字形、凸字形、刀把形、目字形、圆形等七个类型。其中，丰字形、中字形和甲字形为大墓，其余形制皆为外藏坑。秦公陵园的每座陵墓均由若干大墓组成。大墓由土圹和墓道组成，平面呈中字形、甲字形、凸字形、目字形。墓内多发现填泥用炭，有的木炭层厚达3.3至3.8米，外层的青膏泥厚达0.9至2.3米，可见为防潮、防盗而填泥用炭的做法在春秋时期秦国已采用。秦公1号大墓为春秋晚期的秦景公陵寝。该墓平面呈中字形，坐西向东，全长300米，深24米，面积5334平方米，是已发掘的先秦墓葬中最大的一座。椁室中南、北两壁带有柏木榫头的椁木组成长方形框式主椁，是我国古代最早的一套黄肠题凑葬具。椁室两壁外侧的墓碑是中国墓葬史上最早的墓碑实物。墓内186具殉人，是中国自西周以来发现殉人最多的墓葬。咸阳秦陵位于秦都咸阳西北方和东南方。在东西长近10公里、南北宽约7公里的范围内，先后发现战国晚期大型陵园三座，包括惠文王陵、悼武王陵、昭襄王陵、孝文王陵、庄襄王陵、秦始皇陵。秦惠文王、秦悼武王陵位于咸阳西北方，今周陵镇中学附近。陵区有内、外两重陵园，且皆由墙垣和围沟两部分组成，园墙四面各有一门阙遗址。内陵园将南、北二陵界围其中。两陵位于一条南北轴线之上，墓道正对处分别设有门阙。一直以来，认为位于渭城区的南北两座墓是周陵的周文王与周武王之陵。1973年7月，在南陵旁出土了战国圆瓦当两个。同年11月，在北陵西出土了汉砖以及陶片。考古推断南为秦惠文王之陵，北为秦悼武王之陵。南陵封土外形为覆斗状，现高11.8米，底边长约78米，顶边长48米余，墓葬形制为亚字形。北陵南距南陵145.8米，封土外形为截锥体，现存高度12.3米，底边长71米左右，顶边长约41米，墓葬形制为亚字形。临潼秦东陵位于今西安市临潼区韩峪乡东部骊山西麓，南起洪庆沟，北至武家沟。此处先后勘探发现战国秦陵园四座，总面积为24平方公里。一号陵园平面呈长方形，东西长4000米，南北宽1800米，面积72万平方米。陵园内勘探出2座亚字形大墓、陪葬坑2座、陪葬墓2处、地面建筑基址4处。两座亚字形大墓为陵园的主墓，大小相同，主墓道皆为东向；两座陪葬坑分别位于主墓东墓道以东偏南处。二号陵园位于一号陵园东北方向1500米处，韩峪乡范家村北。陵园范围东起北沟村，西到枣园村，南起三家村北无名沟，北达武家沟，东西长500，南北宽300米，总面积为15万平方米。二号陵园内勘探发现有中字形大墓1座、甲字形大墓3座、陪葬坑1座、葬墓区2处、地面建筑1处。三号陵园位于武家沟村北100米处，东南距一号陵园1500米。陵园西、北两侧利用天然壕沟作为其兆沟，东、南两面兆沟为人工开凿。东西长280，南北宽180米，总面积为48400平方米。陵园内有中字形大墓一座，封土呈覆斗形，东西向，西墓道长于东墓道；还发现有陪葬墓区1处、建筑基址2处。四号陵园位于小峪河南岸，整个陵区位于山前冲积扇面上。陵区东起马斜村，西至染房村，南抵井深沟，北到小峪河南岸，与一号陵园隔河相望，相距约2500米，总面积达80万平方米。陵园内发现亚字形大墓1座、甲字形墓葬2座、小型陪葬墓群1处。
projects.content_en: The Qin people were a Huaxia ethnic group that migrated westward during the wars at the end of the Shang Dynasty. In the long historical process of their rise, prosperity, and demise, the Qin people successively built ten mausoleum areas: Xichui, Ya, Pingyang, Yong, Yueyang, Xianyang, Zhiyang, Dudong, Hansenzhai, and Lishan. These construction practices enabled the Qin ancestors to gradually accumulate experience in mausoleum construction, including mausoleum parks, tombs, mounds, ritual buildings, companion tombs, companion pits, and gate towers, ultimately promoting the transformation from centralized public cemeteries to independent mausoleum parks, laying the foundation for the ancient Chinese imperial mausoleum system. The Qin Dukes and Emperors Mausoleum Parks include four major mausoleum areas: Tianshui, Yongcheng, Yueyang, and Xianyang. The mausoleum parks were established from west to east, from Qin and Xichui near Tianshui to Yongcheng, Yueyang, and Xianyang in the Guanzhong area, following the general rule that Qin duke mausoleum parks moved with the capital. Individual emperors were buried in the original capital because the new capital was not yet completed; for example, Duke Xiang and Duke Wen, although they had crossed Longshan, were still buried in the Xichui mausoleum area west of Longshan, and Duke Ling, although moved from Yongcheng to Jingyang, was still buried in Yongcheng. The Yongcheng Qin Dukes Mausoleum Park is located at Nanyuan, Fengxiang County, Baoji City, with a total area of about 21 square kilometers. The entire mausoleum area is about 12 km long east-west and about 3 km wide north-south, with a total area of about 36 square kilometers. On the west, south, and north sides of the mausoleum area, surrounding ditches 2 to 7 m wide and 2 to 6 m deep were found as protective barriers. Each mausoleum park faces east with its back to west, arranged in a wild-goose-feather pattern, with a magnificent scale. It was designated as the third batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1988. The Yongcheng Qin Dukes Mausoleum Park is the largest known burial place of Qin state rulers. Since Duke Mu of Qin, many Qin state rulers should have been buried here. The mausoleum park has a rectangular plane, long north-south and narrow east-west, with protective facilities. The tombs are located in the southern half of the mausoleum park, with sacrificial burial pits to the east; this layout form was also inherited by the later Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Park. Currently, 51 large tombs have been drilled in the Yongcheng Qin Dukes Mausoleum Park, with plane shapes divided into seven types: feng-shaped, zhong-shaped, jia-shaped, tu-shaped, dao-ba-shaped, mu-shaped, and circular. Among them, feng-shaped, zhong-shaped, and jia-shaped are large tombs, while the other shapes are all outer storage pits. Each tomb in the Qin Dukes Mausoleum Park consists of several large tombs. The large tombs consist of earth pits and tomb passages, with planes of zhong-shaped, jia-shaped, tu-shaped, and mu-shaped. In the tombs, mud-filling and charcoal-use were often found; some charcoal layers were 3.3 to 3.8 m thick, and the outer layer of white plaster mud was 0.9 to 2.3 m thick, showing that the practice of filling mud and using charcoal for moisture-proofing and anti-theft was already adopted in the Qin state during the Spring and Autumn period. Qin Duke Tomb No. 1 is the mausoleum of Duke Jing of Qin in the late Spring and Autumn period. This tomb has a zhong-shaped plane, facing east with its back to west, with a total length of 300 m, depth of 24 m, and area of 5,334 square meters, making it the largest excavated pre-Qin tomb. In the coffin chamber, the north and south walls have cypress wood with tenons forming a rectangular frame-style main coffin, which is the earliest set of huangchang ticou (yellow cypress题凑) burial equipment in ancient China. The tomb steles on the outer sides of the two walls of the coffin chamber are the earliest tomb stele实物 in Chinese tomb history. The 186 sacrificial burials in the tomb are the most sacrificial burials discovered in China since the Western Zhou Dynasty. The Xianyang Qin Mausoleums are located northwest and southeast of the Qin capital Xianyang. Within an area nearly 10 km long east-west and about 7 km wide north-south, three large mausoleum parks of the late Warring States period were successively discovered, including the mausoleums of King Huiwen, King Daowu, King Zhaoxiang, King Xiaowen, King Zhuangxiang, and Qin Shi Huang. The mausoleums of King Huiwen and King Daowu of Qin are located northwest of Xianyang, near the current Zhouling Town Middle School. The mausoleum area has inner and outer double mausoleum parks, both composed of wall enclosures and surrounding ditches, with a gate tower site on each of the four sides of the park wall. The inner mausoleum park encloses the south and north mausoleums. The two mausoleums are located on a north-south axis, with gate towers set at the positions directly facing the tomb passages. It has long been believed that the two tombs north and south in Weicheng District are the mausoleums of King Wen and King Wu of Zhou (Zhouling). In July 1973, two Warring States circular tile ends were unearthed beside the south mausoleum. In November of the same year, Han bricks and pottery fragments were unearthed west of the north mausoleum. Archaeological inference: the south is the mausoleum of King Huiwen of Qin, and the north is the mausoleum of King Daowu of Qin. The south mausoleum mound has an inverted-bowl shape, currently 11.8 m high, with a base length of about 78 m and a top length of more than 48 m; the tomb shape is ya-shaped. The north mausoleum is 145.8 m south of the south mausoleum, with a truncated cone-shaped mound, currently 12.3 m high, with a base length of about 71 m and a top length of about 41 m; the tomb shape is ya-shaped. The Lintong Qin East Mausoleums are located at the eastern foot of the west slope of Lishan Mountain, east of Hanyu Township, Lintong District, Xi'an City, starting from Hongqinggou in the south and reaching Wujiaogou in the north. Four Warring States Qin mausoleum parks were successively explored here, with a total area of 24 square kilometers. Mausoleum Park No. 1 has a rectangular plane, 4,000 m long east-west and 1,800 m wide north-south, with an area of 720,000 square meters. In the mausoleum park, 2 ya-shaped large tombs, 2 companion pits, 2 companion tomb areas, and 4 ground building foundation sites were explored. The two ya-shaped large tombs are the main tombs of the mausoleum park, of the same size, with main tomb passages all facing east; the two companion pits are located southeast of the east tomb passages of the main tombs. Mausoleum Park No. 2 is located 1,500 m northeast of Mausoleum Park No. 1, north of Fanjiacun, Hanyu Township. The mausoleum park ranges from Beigou Village in the east to Zaoyuan Village in the west, from Wuminggou north of Sanjiacun in the south to Wujiaogou in the north, 500 m long east-west and 300 m wide north-south, with a total area of 150,000 square meters. In Mausoleum Park No. 2, 1 zhong-shaped large tomb, 3 jia-shaped large tombs, 1 companion pit, 2 companion tomb areas, and 1 ground building were explored. Mausoleum Park No. 3 is located 100 m north of Wujiaogou Village, 1,500 m southeast of Mausoleum Park No. 1. The west and north sides of the mausoleum park use natural ditches as their boundary ditches, while the east and south boundary ditches are artificially dug. It is 280 m long east-west and 180 m wide north-south, with a total area of 48,400 square meters. In the mausoleum park, there is one zhong-shaped large tomb, with an inverted-bowl-shaped mound, facing east-west, with the west tomb passage longer than the east tomb passage; 1 companion tomb area and 2 building foundation sites were also found. Mausoleum Park No. 4 is located on the south bank of the Xiaoyu River, with the entire mausoleum area on a piedmont alluvial fan surface. The mausoleum area ranges from Maxie Village in the east to Ranfang Village in the west, from Jingshen Gou in the south to the south bank of the Xiaoyu River in the north, facing Mausoleum Park No. 1 across the river, about 2,500 m apart, with a total area of 800,000 square meters. In the mausoleum park, 1 ya-shaped large tomb, 2 jia-shaped tombs, and 1 small companion tomb group were found.

projects.name: 秦始皇陵
projects.level: 全国第一批重点文物保护单位、世界文化遗产
projects.address: 西安市临潼区骊山
highlights: 秦始皇陵是中国第一位封建社会皇帝嬴政的陵墓
位于陕西省西安以东31公里处临潼区的骊山
其陵园之制对后世帝王陵园影响极为深远
1961年公布为第一批重点文物保护单位
1987年被联合国教科文组织列入世界文化遗产保护目录
秦始皇墓建于公元前246年至公元前210年
秦始皇去世时仍尚未竣工
其选址受当时礼制文化的影响
地处以昭襄王为中心的芷阳陵区之东
符合长辈居西、晚辈居东的昭穆秩序
秦始皇陵园布置仿秦都咸阳
分为内城周长2.5公里、外城周长6.3公里
开创了中国古代帝王陵制之先河
其中内城垣目前共发现6座城门
内城东西向隔墙上设一门
始皇陵冢位于内城南半部
皇陵封土为覆斗状台体
1962年测量封土的底边南北长350米、东西宽345米、高76米
是中国古代最大的坟丘
内城中封土北侧发现三组大型宫殿建筑群遗址
可能是陵园中陵寝建筑遗迹
即将寝殿从陵上移到墓侧
符合后汉书祭祀志秦始皇出寝

据此判断该建筑群中应有认官遗址

projects.content_zh: 秦始皇陵是中国第一位封建社会皇帝嬴政的陵墓，位于陕西省西安以东31公里处临潼区的骊山，其陵园之制对后世帝王陵园影响极为深远。1961年公布为第一批重点文物保护单位。1987年被联合国教科文组织列入世界文化遗产保护目录。秦始皇墓建于公元前246年至公元前210年，前后费时37年，秦始皇去世时仍尚未竣工。其选址受当时礼制文化的影响，地处以昭襄王为中心的芷阳陵区之东，符合长辈居西、晚辈居东的昭穆秩序。秦始皇陵园布置仿秦都咸阳，布局严整，形制规范。陵园呈长方形，设内、外两重夯土陵墙，分为内城（周长2.5公里）、外城（周长6.3公里），开创了中国古代帝王陵制之先河。其中，内城垣目前共发现6座城门，东、西、南三面各有一门；北垣有二门，内城东西向隔墙上设一门。始皇陵冢位于内城南半部，坐西面东，内置棺椁和陪葬器物，目前尚未发掘。皇陵封土为覆斗状台体，1962年测量封土的底边南北长350米、东西宽345米、高76米，经过多年的风雨侵蚀，今高仍达64米，是中国古代最大的坟丘。内城中封土北侧发现三组大型宫殿建筑群遗址，南北长约750米，东西宽约250米，占地面积18.75万平方米，其建筑密集，规模宏阔。据分析，可能是陵园中陵寝建筑遗迹，即将寝殿从陵上移到墓侧，符合《后汉书·祭祀志》秦始皇出寝，起于墓侧，汉因而弗改的记载。1981、1995年曾考古分别发掘一处建筑群南端的部分基址，出土饮食器皿上刻有丽山认官等陶文，据此判断该建筑群中应有认官遗址。秦始皇陵陪葬坑分布在封土东西两侧。1974年陵东发现规模宏大的三座兵马俑坑，南一北二，呈现倒品字形布局，象征着保卫秦始皇陵的宿卫军。南面的一号坑最大，平面呈矩形，东西长230米...
projects.content_en: The Mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang is the mausoleum of Ying Zheng, the first emperor of feudal China, located at Lishan Mountain in Lintong District, 31 km east of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province. Its mausoleum park system had an extremely profound influence on later imperial mausoleum parks. It was designated as one of the first batch of Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1961. In 1987, it was listed in the World Cultural Heritage Protection Catalog by UNESCO. The tomb of Qin Shi Huang was built from 246 BC to 210 BC, taking 37 years in total, and was still not completed when Qin Shi Huang died. Its site selection was influenced by the ritual culture of the time, located east of the Zhiyang mausoleum area centered on King Zhaoxiang, conforming to the zhao-mu order where elders reside in the west and juniors in the east. The Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Park is arranged imitating the Qin capital Xianyang, with a rigorous layout and standardized form. The mausoleum park is rectangular, with inner and outer double rammed-earth mausoleum walls, divided into an inner city (perimeter 2.5 km) and an outer city (perimeter 6.3 km), pioneering the ancient Chinese imperial mausoleum system. Among them, 6 city gates have currently been found on the inner city wall, with one gate each on the east, west, and south sides; the north wall has two gates, and one gate is set on the east-west partition wall of the inner city. The Qin Shi Huang mausoleum mound is located in the southern half of the inner city, facing east with its back to west, with coffins and burial objects inside, which have not yet been excavated. The imperial mausoleum mound is an inverted-bowl-shaped platform. In 1962, the base of the mound was measured to be 350 m long north-south, 345 m wide east-west, and 76 m high; after years of wind and rain erosion, it is still 64 m high today, making it the largest tomb mound in ancient China. Three groups of large palace building complex sites were found north of the mound in the inner city, about 750 m long north-south and about 250 m wide east-west, covering an area of 187,500 square meters, with dense buildings and a magnificent scale. According to analysis, they may be the remains of mausoleum palace buildings in the mausoleum park, i.e., moving the resting hall from on top of the mausoleum to the side of the tomb, conforming to the record in the 'Book of the Later Han: Treatise on Sacrifices' that 'Qin Shi Huang established the resting hall, starting from the side of the tomb, and the Han dynasty followed it without change.' In 1981 and 1995, archaeological excavations were respectively carried out on part of the foundation sites at the southern end of a building complex, and unearthed food and drink vessels inscribed with pottery scripts such as 'Lishan si guan,' based on which it is judged that there should be a si guan (official in charge of sacrifices) site in this building complex. The companion pits of the Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum are distributed on the east and west sides of the mound. In 1974, three large-scale Terracotta Army pits were found east of the mausoleum, one in the south and two in the north, presenting an inverted pin-character layout, symbolizing the garrison army guarding the Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum. The No. 1 pit in the south is the largest, with a rectangular plane, 230 m long east-west...

highlights: 西汉自高祖刘邦公元前206年称帝到公元8年王莽篡汉
共历高祖、惠帝、文帝、景帝、武帝、昭帝、宣帝、元帝、成帝、哀帝、平帝等11帝214年
汉皇陵皆分布在陕西关中地区
亦即今西安市的东部、东南和北部
其中汉文帝霸陵在今西安市东郊狄寨
汉宣帝杜陵在今西安市东南曲江乡
其余九陵均在渭北咸阳塬上
由西而东为汉武帝茂陵、汉昭帝平陵、汉成帝延陵、汉平帝康陵、汉元帝渭陵、汉哀帝义陵、汉惠帝安陵、汉高祖长陵、汉景帝阳陵
咸阳塬上尚有后妃、贵戚、功臣等陪葬墓冢约1500余座
汉天子即位一年而为陵
西汉帝陵形制属于累土至山
即在地面上夯筑高大的坟丘
除汉文帝霸陵因山为陵、不复起坟
以西南角为最尊长者居处之
帝陵和后陵分布于陵区南部陵园的西部
而陪葬墓区都在帝陵的东北方或东方
迁移豪富居住者用于供奉陵园的县城也营建在帝陵的北方或东方
汉高祖长陵、汉惠帝安陵、汉景帝阳陵、汉武帝茂陵、汉昭帝平陵等五座帝陵均建制陵邑
汉高祖长陵位于今咸阳市渭城区窑店乡三义村附近
目前已发现帝陵、后陵、陵邑、陪葬墓园及大量建筑遗址
1988年列为第三批全国重点文物保护单位
帝陵和后陵在一个陵园内
现仅存南、北、西三面部分城墙
南墙长1245米、西墙长2200米、北墙长200米
长陵陪葬墓的数量为西汉陵墓之最
陪葬墓封土较帝陵而言甚小
形状大略有覆斗形、圆锥形和山形三种
墓冢布局多为南北方阵排列
一组内墓冢又多成对并列
这可能都是同茔异穴的夫妻合葬墓
1960年代发掘的长陵杨家湾陪葬墓及其18座陪葬坑
展现的曲尺形早期汉墓及三千多件彩绘兵马俑
为研究汉代的生活习俗、军制、战阵及武器装备等提供了非常宝贵的资料
汉文帝霸陵位于今西安市灞桥区毛西乡窑远村附近
2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位
是中国历史上第一个依山凿穴为玄宫的帝陵
对六朝及唐代依山为陵的葬制影响极大
汉书文帝纪载汉文帝遗诏
霸陵在白鹿塬的塬头断崖上凿洞为玄宫
墓门、墓道、墓室以石片垒砌
陵园地面陪葬陵冢是文帝之母薄太后
薄太后陵寝位于今西安市东郊狄寨公社鲍旗寨村西北
其封土与陵园遗址均有迹可寻
陵冢四周有夯土筑成的陵园垣墙
因南陵西隔渭水遥望汉高祖长陵
窦皇后陵位于霸陵东南的白鹿塬
其地处南陵之北、窦陵村西北
园内已发现有西汉筒瓦、板瓦、云纹瓦当等大量建筑遗存
推测当时应有较大规模的殿堂建筑
汉景帝阳陵位于今咸阳市渭城区正阳乡张家湾村北塬上
2001年公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位
阳陵陵区由帝陵、后陵、南北区从葬坑、刑徒墓地、陵庙等礼制建筑、陪葬墓及阳陵邑等部分组成
陵区平面呈不规则葫芦形
后陵、南区从葬坑、北区从葬坑、一号建筑基址等距分布于帝陵四角
北区陪葬墓和罗经石遗址位于帝陵南北两侧
刑徒墓地及三处建筑遗址在帝陵西侧
东区陪葬墓园棋盘状分布于帝陵东侧的司马道两侧
阳陵邑则设置在陵园东端
阳陵帝陵陵园平面为正方形
四墙中部均有三出阙门
整个陵园以帝陵为中心
东、南、西、北四侧各有一条墓道
东墓道长69米、南墓道长17米、西墓道长21米、北墓道长23.1米
封土以外分布从葬坑86座
东侧和西侧从葬坑均为东西向分布
南侧和北侧为南北向分布
各坑间距一般在4米左右
阳陵帝陵南阙门遗址由一组两座三出阙相连接构成
三出阙的平面由大小依次递减的三个长方形组成
南北进深分别为25.5、17.4米和11米
阙门的中间为中央门道
门道的两侧为东、西、内、外四塾
塾、主阙台、副阙台皆以砖铺回廊环绕
回廊之外砌有鹅卵石散水
罗经石遗址位于帝陵东南
据推测是景帝陵庙德阳宫的一部分
是阳陵最重要的礼制性建筑之一
也是中国发掘清理面积最大、等级最高的皇家陵园祭祀建筑基址
其正中最高处放置一块方形巨石
巨石用整块黑云母花岗岩石雕凿而成
遗址平面为回字形内外两层
四周有砖铺地面、卵石散水以及大量砖块、瓦片堆积层等遗迹遗物
汉武帝茂陵位于今咸阳兴平市东北约9公里处的南位镇策村南塬上
由于陵区属汉代槐里县茂乡
是修建时间最长、规模最大的西汉皇陵
1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位
茂陵陵园雄踞陵区中心偏东南处
陵园包括由外围墙、外壕沟组成的外城垣及其以内部分组成的区域
包括汉武帝陵园、李夫人墓园、多座建筑遗址、多座外藏坑及9座中型墓葬
东西北三面现存门阙遗址
陵墙及门阙夯土均为平夯
茂陵陵园发现11处建筑遗址
其中汉武帝陵园北墙外司马道两侧发现2处建筑遗址
西侧的8号建筑遗址周围环绕围墙
遗址南部偏西处地面上保存有带二层台的夯土台
底部东西长56.2至57.3米、南北宽40至40.8米、残高5.6米
东侧9号遗址也筑有围墙
疑为汉武帝的便殿遗址
茂陵陪葬墓可确定者113座
李夫人墓东距茂陵约525米
茂陵以东900米处为卫青墓
茂陵东约4000米处为霍光墓
霍去病墓前有大型石刻群
是我国现存早期石雕群中体积最大的石刻艺术品
也是现今唯一见到的西汉陵墓石刻
创作手法上以圆雕为主要表现形式
projects.content_zh: 西汉自高祖刘邦公元前206年称帝到公元8年王莽篡汉，共历高祖、惠帝、文帝、景帝、武帝、昭帝、宣帝、元帝、成帝、哀帝、平帝等11帝214年。汉皇陵皆分布在陕西关中地区，亦即今西安市的东部、东南和北部。其中，汉文帝霸陵在今西安市东郊狄寨，汉宣帝杜陵在今西安市东南曲江乡，二者皆处渭河之南。其余九陵均在渭北咸阳塬上，由西而东为：汉武帝茂陵、汉昭帝平陵、汉成帝延陵、汉平帝康陵、汉元帝渭陵、汉哀帝义陵、汉惠帝安陵、汉高祖长陵、汉景帝阳陵。除上述帝陵外，咸阳塬上尚有后妃、贵戚、功臣等陪葬墓冢约1500余座。西汉盛行厚葬，汉天子即位一年而为陵，其陵墓工程浩大，影响极为深远。诸陵均循古制，因陵均建制陵邑，故咸阳塬又称五陵塬。西汉帝陵形制属于累土至山，即在地面上夯筑高大的坟丘，呈覆斗形。帝、后一般合葬一处，但各有墓冢。除汉文帝霸陵因山为陵、不复起坟，而无封土外，其他均有封土，封土顶未见建筑遗迹。陵园布局为坐西朝东，以西南角为最尊长者居处之，帝陵和后陵分布于陵区南部陵园的西部，而陪葬墓区都在帝陵的东北方或东方。此外，迁移豪富居住者用于供奉陵园的县城也营建在帝陵的北方或东方，称陵邑。汉高祖长陵、汉惠帝安陵、汉景帝阳陵、汉武帝茂陵、汉昭帝平陵等五座帝陵均建制陵邑，故咸阳塬又称五陵塬。汉高祖长陵位于今咸阳市渭城区窑店乡三义村附近，目前已发现帝陵、后陵、陵邑、陪葬墓园及大量建筑遗址。1988年列为第三批全国重点文物保护单位。帝陵为覆斗形，边长135至153米，高32.8米。后陵平面亦为覆斗形，边长130至150米，高30.7米。帝陵和后陵在一个陵园内，帝陵在西，后陵在东。陵园平面为方形，边长780米，周长3120米。陵邑在长陵以北，现仅存南、北、西三面部分城墙，南墙长1245米、西墙长2200米、北墙长200米。西墙上有门址一座，宽15米。陵邑内发现瓦窑一座。长陵陪葬墓的数量为西汉陵墓之最。现存封土堆63处，且皆在长陵以东。陪葬墓封土较帝陵而言甚小，形状大略有覆斗形、圆锥形和山形三种。墓冢布局多为南北方阵排列，成组分布。一组内墓冢又多成对并列，这可能都是同茔异穴的夫妻合葬墓。1960年代发掘的长陵杨家湾陪葬墓及其18座陪葬坑，展现的曲尺形早期汉墓及三千多件彩绘兵马俑，为研究汉代的生活习俗、军制、战阵及武器装备等提供了非常宝贵的资料。汉文帝霸陵位于今西安市灞桥区毛西乡窑远村附近，因灞水而名。2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位。霸陵创薄葬之首，是中国历史上第一个依山凿穴为玄宫的帝陵，对六朝及唐代依山为陵的葬制影响极大。《汉书·文帝纪》载汉文帝遗诏：厚葬以破业，重服以伤生，吾甚不取，治霸陵瓦器，不得以金、银、铜、锡为饰，因其山不起坟。霸陵山川因其故，无有所改。《三辅黄图》云：文帝霸陵因山为藏，不复起坟。霸陵陵园史称盛德园，内建寝殿、便殿等，但目前未见陵园遗迹。据记载，霸陵在白鹿塬的塬头断崖上凿洞为玄宫，内部以石砌筑，并有排水系统，墓门、墓道、墓室以石片垒砌，工程十分浩大。霸陵陪葬墓较少。陵园地面陪葬陵冢是文帝之母薄太后，其妻窦皇后的陵寝。薄太后陵寝位于今西安市东郊狄寨公社鲍旗寨村西北，因在霸陵西南，故称南陵。其封土与陵园遗址均有迹可寻。陵冢呈覆斗形，现高29.5米，周长560米。陵冢四周有夯土筑成的陵园垣墙，垣墙正中建有门阙。因南陵西隔渭水遥望汉高祖长陵，故史书有东望吾子，西望吾夫的说法，当地人称为望子冢。窦皇后陵位于霸陵东南的白鹿塬。其地处南陵之北、窦陵村西北。窦皇后陵在平地起冢，形如覆斗，现高19米，边长137至143米。陵园垣墙为夯土筑成，西墙、南墙遗迹尚存。园内已发现有西汉筒瓦、板瓦、云纹瓦当等大量建筑遗存，推测当时应有较大规模的殿堂建筑。汉景帝阳陵位于今咸阳市渭城区正阳乡张家湾村北塬上。2001年公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位。阳陵陵区由帝陵、后陵、南北区从葬坑、刑徒墓地、陵庙等礼制建筑、陪葬墓及阳陵邑等部分组成。陵区平面呈不规则葫芦形，东西长近6公里，南北宽1至3公里，面积约12平方公里。帝陵坐西面东，居于陵园的中部偏西；后陵、南区从葬坑、北区从葬坑、一号建筑基址等距分布于帝陵四角；北区陪葬墓和罗经石遗址位于帝陵南北两侧，左右对称；刑徒墓地及三处建筑遗址在帝陵西侧，南北一字排列；东区陪葬墓园棋盘状分布于帝陵东侧的司马道两侧；阳陵邑则设置在陵园东端。阳陵帝陵陵园平面为正方形，边长约418米。四边有夯土围墙，墙宽3至3.5米，四墙中部均有三出阙门。整个陵园以帝陵为中心，四角拱卫，南北对称，东西相连，布局规整，结构严谨。陵园中部为封土堆，呈覆斗形，边长约168米，封土高32.28米。帝陵为亚字形，坐西面东。东、南、西、北四侧各有一条墓道，东墓道长69米、南墓道长17米、西墓道长21米、北墓道长23.1米。在帝陵陵园四门以内，封土以外分布从葬坑86座。其中东侧21座，南侧19座，西侧20座，北侧21座，其东北角5座。东侧和西侧从葬坑均为东西向分布，南侧和北侧为南北向分布。各坑间距一般在4米左右。坑的宽度3至4米，绝大多数在3.5米左右。最长的坑超过100米，最短的坑只有4米。坑深3米左右，坑底部距现地表8至14米。阳陵帝陵南阙门遗址由一组两座三出阙相连接构成，三出阙的平面由大小依次递减的三个长方形组成。东西面阔131.5米，南北进深分别为25.5、17.4米和11米。阙门的中间为中央门道，门道的两侧为东、西、内、外四塾，塾外侧是主、副阙台。塾、主阙台、副阙台皆以砖铺回廊环绕，回廊之外砌有鹅卵石散水，内高外低，呈鱼脊形。罗经石遗址位于帝陵东南，据推测是景帝陵庙德阳宫的一部分，是阳陵最重要的礼制性建筑之一，也是中国发掘清理面积最大、等级最高的皇家陵园祭祀建筑基址。遗址地形隆起，外貌呈缓坡状，其正中最高处放置一块方形巨石，故此得名。巨石用整块黑云母花岗岩石雕凿而成，石板上部加工成圆盘，表面刻有十字凹槽，经测定为正南北方向。遗址平面为回字形内外两层，总面积约67000平方米。中心建筑为夯土台基，基座呈正方形，基址边长54米，每边3门，共计12门。四周有砖铺地面、卵石散水以及大量砖块、瓦片堆积层等遗迹遗物。汉武帝茂陵位于今咸阳兴平市东北约9公里处的南位镇策村南塬上，由于陵区属汉代槐里县茂乡，故称茂陵。其营建历时53年，是修建时间最长、规模最大的西汉皇陵。1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。茂陵陵园雄踞陵区中心偏东南处，是整个陵区的核心区。陵园包括由外围墙、外壕沟组成的外城垣及其以内部分组成的区域，包括：汉武帝陵园、李夫人墓园、多座建筑遗址、多座外藏坑及9座中型墓葬。茂陵封土呈覆斗形，现存高48.5米，顶平处边长，东36米，南41.6米，西39.2米，北41.7米，底部边长，东243米，南238米，西243.2米，北240米，与记载基本相符。陵墙东西425.5至433米，南北433.8至435.5米，墙基宽东4.3至6.3米，南4.9至5.2米，西3.8至5.4米，北3.5至5.1米。东西北三面现存门阙遗址，高3至3.5米，门道宽，西门10.7米，北门7.6至9米，东门12米。陵墙及门阙夯土均为平夯，夯层厚4至8厘米，夯窝径8厘米。茂陵陵园发现11处建筑遗址，其中汉武帝陵园北墙外司马道两侧发现2处建筑遗址，西侧的8号建筑遗址周围环绕围墙，形成院落，南墙与陵园北墙共用，南北长244至249.8米、东西宽153米。遗址南部偏西处地面上保存有带二层台的夯土台，底部东西长56.2至57.3米、南北宽40至40.8米、残高5.6米。东侧9号遗址也筑有围墙，南墙与陵园北墙共用，南北长137.3、东西宽82.7至84.7米，疑为汉武帝的便殿遗址。茂陵陪葬墓可确定者113座，尚存封土丘者14座，其中5座有独立墓园，地面现存封土共12座。李夫人墓东距茂陵约525米，墓冢外形为两层台，又称为英陵。茂陵以东900米处为卫青墓，其东南方为霍去病墓，东北方为金日磾墓，茂陵东约4000米处为霍光墓。其中，霍去病墓前有大型石刻群，是我国现存早期石雕群中体积最大的石刻艺术品，也是现今唯一见到的西汉陵墓石刻。创作手法上以圆雕为主要表现形式，辅以浮雕、线刻等，作品方中见圆，以静带动，拙中见巧，生动自然，气魄深沉雄大。
projects.content_en: The Western Han dynasty, from Emperor Gaozu Liu Bang's ascension in 206 BC to Wang Mang's usurpation in 8 AD, lasted 214 years through 11 emperors: Gaozu, Huidi, Wendi, Jingdi, Wudi, Zhaodi, Xuandi, Yuandi, Chengdi, Aidi, and Pingdi. The Han imperial mausoleums are all distributed in the Guanzhong area of Shaanxi, i.e., the eastern, southeastern, and northern parts of present-day Xi'an. Among them, Emperor Wen's Baling is in present-day Dizhai, eastern suburb of Xi'an, and Emperor Xuan's Duling is in present-day Qujiang Township, southeast of Xi'an, both located south of the Wei River. The other nine mausoleums are all on the Xianyang Plateau north of the Wei River, from west to east: Emperor Wu's Maoling, Emperor Zhao's Pingling, Emperor Cheng's Yanling, Emperor Ping's Kangling, Emperor Yuan's Weiling, Emperor Ai's Yiling, Emperor Hui's Anling, Emperor Gaozu's Changling, and Emperor Jing's Yangling. In addition to the above imperial mausoleums, there are about 1,500 or more companion tomb mounds of empresses, nobles, and meritorious officials on the Xianyang Plateau. The Western Han dynasty盛行 lavish burials; 'the Han emperor begins building his mausoleum one year after ascending the throne,' with massive mausoleum engineering and extremely profound influence. All mausoleums followed ancient systems, and because mausoleum towns were established for each, the Xianyang Plateau is also called the 'Five Mausoleum Plateau.' The Western Han imperial mausoleum form belongs to 'piling earth to form a mountain,' i.e., ramming tall tomb mounds on the ground, in an inverted-bowl shape. Emperors and empresses were generally buried together in one place but each had their own tomb mound. Except for Emperor Wen's Baling, which 'used the mountain as the mausoleum and did not raise a mound' and thus had no mound, all others had mounds, with no building remains found on top of the mounds. The mausoleum park layout faces east with its back to west, 'with the southwest corner as the residence of the most venerable elder'; the emperor's and empress's mausoleums are distributed in the western part of the southern mausoleum park of the mausoleum area, while the companion tomb areas are all northeast or east of the emperor's mausoleum. In addition, the towns where wealthy people were relocated to live to serve the mausoleum parks were also built north or east of the emperor's mausoleums, called 'mausoleum towns.' Five imperial mausoleums—Emperor Gaozu's Changling, Emperor Hui's Anling, Emperor Jing's Yangling, Emperor Wu's Maoling, and Emperor Zhao's Pingling—all established mausoleum towns, hence the Xianyang Plateau is also called the Five Mausoleum Plateau. Emperor Gaozu's Changling is located near Sanyi Village, Yaodian Township, Weicheng District, Xianyang City. Currently, the emperor's mausoleum, empress's mausoleum, mausoleum town, companion tomb parks, and many building sites have been found. It was listed as the third batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1988. The emperor's mausoleum is inverted-bowl shaped, with side lengths of 135 to 153 m and height of 32.8 m. The empress's mausoleum plane is also inverted-bowl shaped, with side lengths of 130 to 150 m and height of 30.7 m. The emperor's and empress's mausoleums are in one mausoleum park, with the emperor's in the west and the empress's in the east. The mausoleum park plane is square, with a side length of 780 m and perimeter of 3,120 m. The mausoleum town is north of Changling; currently only partial city walls on the south, north, and west sides remain, with the south wall 1,245 m long, west wall 2,200 m long, and north wall 200 m long. There is one gate site on the west wall, 15 m wide. A tile kiln was found in the mausoleum town. The number of companion tombs at Changling is the greatest among Western Han mausoleums. There are currently 63 existing mound sites, all east of Changling. The companion tomb mounds are much smaller than the emperor's mausoleum, with shapes roughly of three types: inverted-bowl, conical, and mountain-shaped. The tomb mounds are mostly arranged in north-south formations, distributed in groups. Within a group, the tomb mounds are often paired side by side, which may all be husband-and-wife joint burials in the same grave plot but separate tombs. The Yangjiawan companion tombs of Changling and their 18 companion pits excavated in the 1960s, showing the curved-foot-shaped early Han tombs and more than 3,000 painted terracotta warriors and horses, provided very valuable materials for studying Han dynasty life customs, military systems, battle formations, and weapons and equipment. Emperor Wen's Baling is located near Yaoyuan Village, Maoxi Township, Baqiao District, Xi'an City, named after the Ba River. It was designated as the fifth batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 2001. Baling pioneered 'frugal burial' and is the first imperial mausoleum in Chinese history to chisel a cave into the mountain as the underground palace, having an extremely great influence on the mountain-based burial system of the Six Dynasties and Tang dynasty. The 'Book of Han: Annals of Emperor Wen' records Emperor Wen's testamentary edict: 'Lavish burial ruins the estate, heavy mourning harms the living; I very much do not approve. Build Baling with pottery vessels, do not decorate with gold, silver, copper, or tin; use the mountain as it is, do not raise a mound.' 'The mountains and rivers of Baling follow their original form, with no alterations.' The 'Sanfu Huangtu' says: 'Emperor Wen's Baling used the mountain as the storage, did not raise a mound.' The Baling mausoleum park was historically called the Shengde Garden, with resting halls and side halls built inside, but currently no mausoleum park remains have been found. According to records, Baling chiseled caves into the cliff at the edge of the Bailu Plateau as the underground palace, with the interior built of stone, and a drainage system; the tomb gates, passages, and chambers were laid with stone slabs, with a very massive project. Baling has fewer companion tombs. The above-ground companion tomb mounds in the mausoleum park are the mausoleums of Empress Dowager Bo (Emperor Wen's mother) and Empress Dou (his wife). Empress Dowager Bo's mausoleum is located northwest of Baoqizhai Village, Dizhai Commune, eastern suburb of Xi'an; because it is southwest of Baling, it is called the South Mausoleum. Its mound and mausoleum park sites are both traceable. The tomb mound is inverted-bowl shaped, currently 29.5 m high and 560 m in circumference. Around the tomb mound, there are rammed-earth mausoleum park walls, with gate towers built in the center of the walls. Because the South Mausoleum faces Emperor Gaozu's Changling across the Wei River to the west, historical records say 'looking east to my son, looking west to my husband,' and locals call it the Wangzi Tomb (Tomb Looking at the Son). Empress Dou's mausoleum is located on the Bailu Plateau southeast of Baling, north of the South Mausoleum and northwest of Douling Village. Empress Dou's mausoleum raised a mound on flat ground, shaped like an inverted bowl, currently 19 m high with side lengths of 137 to 143 m. The mausoleum park walls are built of rammed earth, with remains of the west and south walls still existing. A large number of Western Han building remains such as tube tiles, flat tiles, and cloud-pattern tile ends have been found in the park,推测 that there should have been relatively large-scale hall buildings at that time. Emperor Jing's Yangling is located on the plateau north of Zhangjiawan Village, Zhengyang Township, Weicheng District, Xianyang City. It was designated as the third batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 2001. The Yangling mausoleum area consists of the emperor's mausoleum, empress's mausoleum, north and south burial pits, convict cemetery, ritual buildings such as mausoleum temples, companion tombs, and Yangling Town. The mausoleum area plane is irregularly gourd-shaped, nearly 6 km long east-west, 1 to 3 km wide north-south, with an area of about 12 square kilometers. The emperor's mausoleum faces east with its back to west, located slightly west of the center of the mausoleum park; the empress's mausoleum, south burial pits, north burial pits, and No. 1 building foundation are equidistantly distributed at the four corners of the emperor's mausoleum; the north companion tombs and Luojingshi site are located on the north and south sides of the emperor's mausoleum, symmetrical left and right; the convict cemetery and three building sites are west of the emperor's mausoleum, arranged in a north-south line; the east companion tomb parks are distributed in a checkerboard pattern on both sides of the Sima Road east of the emperor's mausoleum; Yangling Town is set at the eastern end of the mausoleum park. The Yangling emperor's mausoleum park plane is square, with a side length of about 418 m. There are rammed-earth walls on all four sides, 3 to 3.5 m wide, with triple gate towers in the center of each wall. The entire mausoleum park centers on the emperor's mausoleum, with the four corners guarding, north-south symmetry, east-west connection, a regular layout, and a rigorous structure. In the center of the mausoleum park is the mound, inverted-bowl shaped, with a side length of about 168 m and mound height of 32.28 m. The emperor's mausoleum is ya-shaped, facing east with its back to west. There is one tomb passage on each of the east, south, west, and north sides, with the east passage 69 m long, south passage 17 m long, west passage 21 m long, and north passage 23.1 m long. Within the four gates of the emperor's mausoleum park and outside the mound, 86 burial pits are distributed. Among them, 21 on the east side, 19 on the south side, 20 on the west side, 21 on the north side, and 5 at its northeast corner. The east and west burial pits are all distributed east-west, while the south and north are distributed north-south. The spacing between pits is generally about 4 m. The pit width is 3 to 4 m, with the vast majority about 3.5 m. The longest pit exceeds 100 m, and the shortest pit is only 4 m. The pit depth is about 3 m, and the pit bottom is 8 to 14 m from the current ground surface. The Yangling emperor's mausoleum south gate tower site consists of a pair of connected triple gate towers; the plane of the triple gate tower consists of three rectangles decreasing in size sequentially. It is 131.5 m wide east-west, with north-south depths of 25.5, 17.4, and 11 m respectively. The center of the gate tower is the central passage, and on both sides of the passage are four side rooms—east, west, inner, and outer—with the main and secondary gate platforms outside the side rooms. The side rooms, main gate platforms, and secondary gate platforms are all surrounded by brick-paved corridors, and outside the corridors, cobblestone drainage aprons are laid, high inside and low outside, in a fish-ridge shape. The Luojingshi site is located southeast of the emperor's mausoleum; it is推测 to be part of the Deyang Palace, Emperor Jing's mausoleum temple, and is one of the most important ritual buildings of Yangling, as well as the largest and highest-ranking royal mausoleum park sacrificial building foundation excavated and cleared in China. The site terrain is raised, with a gently sloping appearance; at its highest center, a square boulder is placed, hence the name. The boulder is carved from a whole piece of biotite granite, with the upper part of the stone slab processed into a disc, with cross grooves carved on the surface, measured to be due north-south. The site plane is hui-shaped (回字形) with inner and outer two layers, with a total area of about 67,000 square meters. The central building is a rammed-earth platform, with a square base, 54 m on each side, 3 gates on each side, totaling 12 gates. Around it are brick-paved ground, cobblestone drainage aprons, and a large number of remains and relics such as brick and tile accumulation layers. Emperor Wu's Maoling is located on the plateau south of Cewu Village, Nanwei Town, about 9 km northeast of Xingping City, Xianyang. Because the mausoleum area belonged to Maoxiang, Huaili County in the Han dynasty, it is called Maoling. Its construction lasted 53 years, making it the longest-built and largest-scale Western Han imperial mausoleum. It was designated as one of the first batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1961. The Maoling mausoleum park occupies the center-southeast of the mausoleum area and is the core area of the entire mausoleum area. The mausoleum park includes the outer city wall composed of the outer wall and outer ditch and the area within it, including: Emperor Wu's mausoleum park, Lady Li's tomb park, multiple building sites, multiple outer storage pits, and 9 medium-sized tombs. The Maoling mound is inverted-bowl shaped, currently 48.5 m high; the flat top side lengths are: east 36 m, south 41.6 m, west 39.2 m, north 41.7 m; the bottom side lengths are: east 243 m, south 238 m, west 243.2 m, north 240 m, basically consistent with records. The mausoleum walls are 425.5 to 433 m east-west and 433.8 to 435.5 m north-south; the wall base widths are: east 4.3 to 6.3 m, south 4.9 to 5.2 m, west 3.8 to 5.4 m, north 3.5 to 5.1 m. Gate tower sites currently exist on the east, west, and north sides, 3 to 3.5 m high; the passage widths are: west gate 10.7 m, north gate 7.6 to 9 m, east gate 12 m. The rammed earth of the mausoleum walls and gate towers is all flat rammed, with rammed layers 4 to 8 cm thick and rammed pits 8 cm in diameter. Eleven building sites were found in the Maoling mausoleum park, among which 2 building sites were found on both sides of the Sima Road outside the north wall of Emperor Wu's mausoleum park; the No. 8 building site on the west side is surrounded by walls, forming a courtyard, with the south wall shared with the north wall of the mausoleum park, 244 to 249.8 m long north-south and 153 m wide east-west. On the ground slightly west of the south part of the site, a rammed-earth platform with two tiers is preserved, with the bottom 56.2 to 57.3 m long east-west, 40 to 40.8 m wide north-south, and 5.6 m remaining height. The No. 9 site on the east side also has walls, with the south wall shared with the north wall of the mausoleum park, 137.3 m long north-south and 82.7 to 84.7 m wide east-west, suspected to be the site of Emperor Wu's side hall. 113 companion tombs at Maoling can be确定, with 14 still having mound sites, among which 5 have independent mausoleum parks, and 12 mounds currently exist on the ground. Lady Li's tomb is about 525 m east of Maoling, with a two-tiered tomb mound shape, also called the Ying Mausoleum. 900 m east of Maoling is Wei Qing's tomb, southeast of it is Huo Qubing's tomb, northeast is Jin Midi's tomb, and about 4,000 m east of Maoling is Huo Guang's tomb. Among them, in front of Huo Qubing's tomb there is a large stone carving group, which is the largest-volume stone carving artwork among existing early stone carving groups in China, and also the only Western Han mausoleum stone carvings seen today. The creative technique uses round carving as the main form, supplemented by relief and line carving; the works show roundness within squareness, movement within stillness, cleverness within clumsiness, vivid and natural, with a deep and grand spirit.

projects.name: 唐代帝陵（昭陵、乾陵、泰陵、贞陵）
projects.name_en: Tang Imperial Mausoleums (Zhaoling, Qianling, Tailing, Zhenling)
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位
projects.address: 咸阳市礼泉县、乾县、蒲城县、泾阳县
highlights: 唐朝自高祖李渊公元618年称帝到唐哀帝李柷公元907年禅位
共历高祖、太宗、高宗、玄宗等21帝289年
因武则天与唐高宗合葬
除昭宗和陵、哀帝温陵两座陵墓外
其余18座均位于陕西关中地区
其东起蒲城、富平、三原、泾阳、礼泉
唐陵基本形制可分为两类
一种是建于高塬的覆斗形土冢
包括营建于三原县荆塬和徐木塬之上的献、庄、端三陵
以及建于乾县北塬之上的靖陵
其所在地海拔皆在500至800米以上
另一种是利用渭北岛伏山丘地带的自然山势
其他诸陵则完全由山下凿成阶梯式的墓道
唐陵陵园形制发展演变大致可分为四个阶段
第一阶段为初唐时期的昭陵、献陵
属于借鉴汉魏帝陵制度的探索阶段
但其设计对后来者产生深远影响
如昭陵首创因山为陵之风
昭陵六骏、十四国蕃君长石像则成为历代唐陵园石刻中置蕃酋石像及北门石马的先例
献陵的方形陵园、神道石刻的石柱、陪葬墓分布在陵园东侧
第二阶段为盛唐时期的乾陵、定陵、桥陵
标志唐代帝陵陵园形制的正式形成
陵园平面布局尽量设计成方形
下宫安排在乳台阙与鹊台阙之间的神道西侧
陪葬墓分布在神道东侧
陵园石刻组合基本形成定制
继承了第一阶段石刻体量较大的特点
第三阶段基本沿袭盛唐时期陵园布局
又产生一些新的调整和变化
因山为陵的陵园平面不再追求方形布局
神道两侧石人分为左文右武
第四阶段唐代帝陵制度走向衰微
阙台亦不再使用三出阙形式
唐太宗昭陵位于今咸阳市礼泉县城东北22公里处的九嵕山主峰
陵墓营建始于贞观十年公元636年
至贞观二十三年公元649年基本结束
1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位
昭陵开创了帝王因山为陵之制
唐会要载太宗谓侍臣曰
史载昭陵因山凿石为元宫墓室
从埏道墓道至墓室深75丈
又因山势陡峭、往来不便
昭陵陵园为唐王朝诸帝陵园中最大者
纵横昭陵、烟霞、赵镇、北屯4个乡镇
约占整个礼泉县的五分之一
内城北面有祭坛和玄武门
门内列置当时少数民族首领石刻像14座
昭陵六骏石刻即为东西室内遗物
现主要建筑群遗址存留三处
一为九嵕山南侧偏东的南神门及献殿遗址
一为西南侧的寝宫遗址
一为北侧北司马门遗址
此外还有山腰南侧和东侧的石窟、石室遗迹
北司马门是一组完整的南北向轴对称建筑群
南北长86米、东西最宽处61米
分布于九嵕山北侧山梁的三个小台地上
整个遗址所处地势呈南高北低的状态
建筑遗迹由南向北逐渐升高
依次为第一台地上的三出阙的台基一对、推测为列戟的廊址、北围墙外的小型建筑4座
第二台地的北边缘是庑殿式门址和北围墙、砖砌排水沟等
从南向北依次为偏殿、方形小建筑、阶梯状长廊等
建筑群外环绕带砖铺散水的夯土墙
也只有西侧保留有部分墙基
建筑群的最北端为东西双阙
阙底部周绕宽85厘米的砖砌散水
九嵕山南侧、东侧的山坡及山下平原地带为昭陵陪葬墓区
其陪葬墓数量、规模、形制当属唐朝诸帝陵之冠
反映了封建王朝上升时期的磅礴气势与等级森严的社会制度
陪葬墓有依山凿为墓室
有起冢作覆斗形、圆锥状
墓前多有石人、石羊、石虎、石碑
这些墓葬大体按时间先后
而陵墓高度则按官位品第有所限定
乾陵为唐高宗与武则天的合葬墓
位于今咸阳市乾县城西北6公里处的梁山
乾陵营建始于唐高宗去世
弘道元年公元683年唐高宗死于洛阳
文明元年公元684年葬于乾陵
神龙元年公元705年武则天死于洛阳
神龙二年公元706年合葬于乾陵
1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位
因梁山位于长安西北的乾位
乾县县城西北1.5公里的张家堡处
两侧石刻有石华表一对
华表在古代为帝王纳谏的象征
石人之北13.5米处有述圣纪碑在西
为当时参加葬礼的外国首领使臣像
石狮北为献殿遗址所在
乾陵的石刻群制式对后面的其他皇陵都产生了一些影响
如唐肃宗建陵以及唐睿宗桥陵都因袭了乾陵的定制
乾陵陵园借自然山峰而建
梁山北峰是乾陵地宫所在
围绕北峰修筑高大的城垣称为宫城
朱雀门外利用低凹地带修筑宽阔神道
两乳峰之间形成陵园天然门户
它与神道两侧的华表、翼马、朱雀、石人等石雕艺术品
共同营建了陵前建筑环境
与地宫上的天然山峰北峰
墓道及墓门位于山南面中腰部
系于天然石灰岩山上凿成
由东向西657米处有高出地面1米、径10米的夯土墩遗迹
南城墙经过黄巢沟均修有走水洞
西北、东北城角有石条砌筑的地基存在
乾陵陵域内分布17座陪葬墓
懿德太子李重润号墓为陵
是已发掘的规模最大、等级最高的唐陵皇室陪葬墓之一
永泰公主李先蕙墓亦号墓为陵
是唐212位公主中唯一享受此规格待遇的墓主
也是发掘最早、等级较高的唐代女性皇室墓葬
章怀太子李贤在迁葬时
唐玄宗泰陵位于蒲城县城东北15公里处的金粟山
2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位
金粟山东西4.2公里、南北2公里
墓室位于南北门中轴线上
东西两门分别设于西峰自山顶左右延伸的山脊之上
除南门位于山前缓坡地外
东、西、北三门均筑于山脊或山坡台地上
如西南角阙至东南角阙直线距离1176.9米
而西北角阙至东北角阙直线距离仅为765.3米
城垣平面约略呈不规则的五边形
其他三面的墙垣都非直线延伸
北垣墙由西北角阙开始折向东北方向与北门相接后
再与距离较近的东北角阙相接
西垣墙修建在山梁西侧的坡地上
东墙垣基本是沿着山脊走向蜿蜒起伏
泰陵地面建筑有献殿、下宫、陵署等
据唐会要、长安志、文献通考及关中陵墓志记载只有一座
即已经发掘的高力士墓
泰陵石刻整体保存数量较多
泰陵石刻不包括蕃酋像原应有50件组
仗马、底座与牵马人按一组算
包括南门神道西侧第四仗马底座、蕃酋像残块4件、蕃酋像底座1件
北门神道东侧第三仗马包括仗马和底座、牵马人和西侧第一仗马包括仗马和底座
北门还出土石虎1件以及石人毛坯1件
唐宣宗贞陵位于泾阳县白王乡崔黄村北的北仲山
2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位
贞陵陵园南北跨泾阳、淳化两县
地表仅存鹊台遗址、角阙遗址和各门前土阙及地面石刻
其布局呈南窄北宽的不规则形状
除南门位于较平缓的北仲山南麓外
其余三门均筑于山脊上
南墙垣地处山下较为平缓的地带
西墙垣从西南角阙向北沿山脊蜿蜒通向西门
然后向西北方向沿山脊与西北角阙相接
东墙垣从东南角阙向北坡度较缓
东门以北则沿山脊蜿蜒至东北角阙
西部明显向西南的山脊延伸
与东北、西北角阙连接均需经陡坡和沟壑
贞陵下宫遗址位于泾阳县白王镇庙背后村北部的台地上
宫城整体平面呈长方形
建筑遗迹破坏较为严重
较大的夯土基址有两处
两处建筑基址与南门均在宫城的中轴线上
贞陵神道石刻群自南向北依次为
在南门阙以南的蕃酋殿建筑遗址出土蕃酋石人像6件
贞陵北门石刻除石狮1对
相比较乾陵的石刻群而言
其石刻群雕凿较为粗糙

唐朝自高祖李渊公元618年称帝到唐哀帝李柷公元907年禅位，共历高祖、太宗、高宗、玄宗等21帝289年。因武则天与唐高宗合葬，故唐王陵共计20座。除昭宗和陵、哀帝温陵两座陵墓外，其余18座均位于陕西关中地区，其东起蒲城、富平、三原、泾阳、礼泉，西止乾县，东西横亘150公里，人称关中十八陵。唐陵基本形制可分为两类：一种是建于高塬的覆斗形土冢，包括营建于三原县荆塬和徐木塬之上的献、庄、端三陵，以及建于乾县北塬之上的靖陵，其所在地海拔皆在500至800米以上，塬高土厚，便于深埋。另一种是利用渭北岛伏山丘地带的自然山势，于山南开凿墓室成陵，其海拔约1200至1600米，因范围宏大、形势壮观，故有山陵之称，其余14座唐陵皆属此类。如昭陵南临悬崖峭壁，故缘山傍岩，架梁为栈道，通至墓门。其他诸陵则完全由山下凿成阶梯式的墓道，达于墓门。埋葬之后，一无形迹，欲使易代之后，不知其处，并定为制度，世代沿袭。唐陵陵园形制发展演变大致可分为四个阶段：第一阶段为初唐时期的昭陵、献陵，属于借鉴汉魏帝陵制度的探索阶段。彼时，陵园布局尚未定制，故而形制截然不同，但其设计对后来者产生深远影响。如昭陵首创因山为陵之风，昭陵六骏、十四国蕃君长石像则成为历代唐陵园石刻中置蕃酋石像及北门石马的先例。献陵的方形陵园、神道石刻的石柱、陪葬墓分布在陵园东侧，也为其后帝陵所采用。第二阶段为盛唐时期的乾陵、定陵、桥陵，标志唐代帝陵陵园形制的正式形成。陵园平面布局尽量设计成方形，局部因地势稍作调整。神道向南设置三重阙，下宫安排在乳台阙与鹊台阙之间的神道西侧，陪葬墓分布在神道东侧。陵园石刻组合基本形成定制，种类、数量急剧增加，形体高大，排列有序。继承了第一阶段石刻体量较大的特点，南门狮一般高2.7至3米，石人通常高4米左右。第三阶段基本沿袭盛唐时期陵园布局，如泰陵乾陵模式，又产生一些新的调整和变化。从泰陵开始，因山为陵的陵园平面不再追求方形布局，多随地势灵活调整，往往呈不规则形。神道两侧石人分为左文右武，石刻个体变小，如门外石狮高1.5至1.7米，石人通常高2.5至2.9米。下宫规模减小，陪葬墓数量减少。第四阶段唐代帝陵制度走向衰微。除贞陵外，陵园规模逐渐变小，阙台亦不再使用三出阙形式。石刻组合基本稳定，石刻体量更趋变小，至靖陵时，石狮高度不足1米，石人高度不足2米，陪葬制度渐趋消失。唐太宗昭陵位于今咸阳市礼泉县城东北22公里处的九嵕山主峰。陵墓营建始于贞观十年（公元636年），至贞观二十三年（公元649年）基本结束，历时13年。1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。昭陵开创了帝王因山为陵之制。《唐会要》载：太宗谓侍臣曰：古者因山为坟，此诚便事，我看九嵕山孤耸回绕，因而傍凿，可置山陵处。九嵕山主峰山势突兀，海拔1888米，东西两侧层峦起伏，泾水环绕其后，渭河萦带于前，更显得气势宏伟。既因山势，虽不起坟，自然高敞。史载昭陵因山凿石为元宫（墓室），从埏道（墓道）至墓室深75丈，前后置五道石门。为使宫人供养如平常，还在山上建房舍。又因山势陡峭、往来不便，则缘山傍岩，架梁为栈道，悬绝百仞，绕山二百三十步，始达元宫门。昭陵陵园为唐王朝诸帝陵园中最大者，其南北长12.65公里，东西长15.45公里，纵横昭陵、烟霞、赵镇、北屯4个乡（镇），面积113.15平方公里，约占整个礼泉县的五分之一。陵园为内、外二城，内城为方形，四面筑有围墙，并各开城门一座。内城北面有祭坛和玄武门，门内列置当时少数民族首领石刻像14座，现仅存4座；门内设东西室，昭陵六骏石刻即为东西室内遗物。现主要建筑群遗址存留三处：一为九嵕山南侧偏东的南神门及献殿遗址，一为西南侧的寝宫遗址，一为北侧北司马门遗址。此外还有山腰南侧和东侧的石窟、石室遗迹。北司马门是一组完整的南北向轴对称建筑群，南北长86米、东西最宽处61米，分布于九嵕山北侧山梁的三个小台地上，整个遗址所处地势呈南高北低的状态，东西两侧是沟壑。建筑遗迹由南向北逐渐升高，依次为第一台地上的三出阙的台基一对、推测为列戟的廊址、北围墙外的小型建筑4座；第二台地的北边缘是庑殿式门址和北围墙、砖砌排水沟等；第二台地以上，仅残存西侧建筑遗迹，从南向北依次为偏殿、方形小建筑、阶梯状长廊等。建筑群外环绕带砖铺散水的夯土墙，也只有西侧保留有部分墙基。建筑群的最北端为东西双阙，两阙间距31.5米，仅存阙台下部，形制相同，内为夯土台基，外围包砌砖壁。阙底部周绕宽85厘米的砖砌散水，与阙体相应成三出状。九嵕山南侧、东侧的山坡及山下平原地带为昭陵陪葬墓区，据统计共有198座陪葬墓。其陪葬墓数量、规模、形制当属唐朝诸帝陵之冠，反映了封建王朝上升时期的磅礴气势与等级森严的社会制度。陪葬墓有依山凿为墓室，有起冢作覆斗形、圆锥状，以象山形，也有不封不树；墓前多有石人、石羊、石虎、石碑。这些墓葬大体按时间先后，由北向南作自然排列，而陵墓高度则按官位品第有所限定。乾陵为唐高宗与武则天的合葬墓，位于今咸阳市乾县城西北6公里处的梁山。乾陵营建始于唐高宗去世。弘道元年（公元683年）唐高宗死于洛阳，文明元年（公元684年）葬于乾陵；神龙元年（公元705年）武则天死于洛阳，神龙二年（公元706年）合葬于乾陵。1961年公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位。乾陵选址甚佳。梁山东距长安80公里，九嵕处其东，武水环其西，北连丘陵，南接平原，孤峰特起，挺拔俊秀，是建陵的理想之地。因梁山位于长安西北的乾位，故将陵墓定名为乾陵。乾陵陵园布局严整。乾县县城西北1.5公里的张家堡处，有两座8米高的土丘，为乾陵第一门道遗迹；北行3公里为南二峰；从二峰向北为神道，两侧石刻有石华表一对（华表在古代为帝王纳谏的象征）、飞马一对、朱雀一对、石马五对（其中有控马人三对）、两手握剑石人十对；石人之北13.5米处有述圣纪碑（在西）与无字碑（在东）；其后有石人61尊，为当时参加葬礼的外国首领使臣像；朱雀门在梁山南麓，门前有石狮一对，石狮北为献殿遗址所在。乾陵的石刻群制式对后面的其他皇陵都产生了一些影响，如唐肃宗建陵以及唐睿宗桥陵都因袭了乾陵的定制。乾陵陵园借自然山峰而建。梁山北峰是乾陵地宫所在。围绕北峰修筑高大的城垣称为宫城，四面均辟一门，门外设置石刻和阙楼。朱雀门外利用低凹地带修筑宽阔神道，其南端直抵乳峰脚下。两乳峰之间形成陵园天然门户，乳峰之巅建阙楼。它与神道两侧的华表、翼马、朱雀、石人等石雕艺术品，共同营建了陵前建筑环境，与地宫上的天然山峰——北峰，形成强烈的空间对比。墓道及墓门位于山南面中腰部，系于天然石灰岩山上凿成。墓道呈南北向斜坡，全长约65米，东西宽3.87米。乾陵原有内外二重城，内城城基遗迹尚存。其南城基长1438米，由东向西657米处有高出地面1米、径10米的夯土墩遗迹，为朱雀门遗址。南城墙经过黄巢沟均修有走水洞，用石条砌筑。北城基长1450米，东城基长1582米，西城基长1450米，城基夯土宽2.1至2.5米。城角遗迹，东南城角高7.5米，东北城角高5.1米，西北城角高5.5米，西南城角高10米，均为夯土筑成。西北、东北城角有石条砌筑的地基存在。乾陵陵域内分布17座陪葬墓。其中，懿德太子李重润号墓为陵，是已发掘的规模最大、等级最高的唐陵皇室陪葬墓之一。永泰公主李先蕙墓亦号墓为陵，是唐212位公主中唯一享受此规格待遇的墓主，也是发掘最早、等级较高的唐代女性皇室墓葬。章怀太子李贤在迁葬时，以雍王礼陪葬，等级最低。唐玄宗泰陵位于蒲城县城东北15公里处的金粟山。2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位。金粟山东西4.2公里、南北2公里，分东、西两座较大山峰。泰陵陵园将西峰环绕，东西1.2公里、南北1.3公里，平面大致呈方形，墓室位于南北门中轴线上，东西两门分别设于西峰自山顶左右延伸的山脊之上。泰陵因山为陵，凿墓室于山腹中，依山麓绕筑陵墙，分内、外城。内城垣四面原辟四门，受地形限制，四门选址因地而宜，并非对称布局。除南门位于山前缓坡地外，东、西、北三门均筑于山脊或山坡台地上，地域狭小。东、西两门直线间距1168.8米，南、北两门直线间距1133.8米。城垣四角各有角阙，角阙之间距离悬殊，如西南角阙至东南角阙直线距离1176.9米，而西北角阙至东北角阙直线距离仅为765.3米。受地形影响，城垣平面约略呈不规则的五边形。除南垣墙较直外，其他三面的墙垣都非直线延伸。北垣墙由西北角阙开始折向东北方向与北门相接后，再与距离较近的东北角阙相接；西垣墙修建在山梁西侧的坡地上，大致呈弧形；东墙垣基本是沿着山脊走向蜿蜒起伏，呈蛇行状。泰陵地面建筑有献殿、下宫、陵署等，今已无存。其陪葬墓，据《唐会要》《长安志》《文献通考》及《关中陵墓志》记载只有一座，即已经发掘的高力士墓。泰陵石刻整体保存数量较多，但保存状况较差。泰陵石刻（不包括蕃酋像）原应有50件（组）（仗马、底座与牵马人按一组算），地面现存41件（组）。新清理出土石刻9件（组），包括南门神道西侧第四仗马底座、蕃酋像残块4件、蕃酋像底座1件，北门神道东侧第三仗马（包括仗马和底座、牵马人）和西侧第一仗马（包括仗马和底座），北门还出土石虎1件以及石人毛坯1件。唐宣宗贞陵位于泾阳县白王乡崔黄村北的北仲山。2001年公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位。贞陵陵园南北跨泾阳、淳化两县。园内地貌复杂，山势陡峭，地表仅存鹊台遗址、角阙遗址和各门前土阙及地面石刻。陵园城垣环北仲山，依自然山势而筑。其布局呈南窄北宽的不规则形状，除南门位于较平缓的北仲山南麓外，其余三门均筑于山脊上。城基属夯筑，南墙垣地处山下较为平缓的地带，呈直线延伸；西墙垣从西南角阙向北沿山脊蜿蜒通向西门，然后向西北方向沿山脊与西北角阙相接；东墙垣从东南角阙向北坡度较缓，取直线通向东门，东门以北则沿山脊蜿蜒至东北角阙；北墙垣地形最为复杂，西部明显向西南的山脊延伸，与东北、西北角阙连接均需经陡坡和沟壑，起伏较大。贞陵下宫遗址位于泾阳县白王镇庙背后村北部的台地上，东南距西鹊台遗址299.24米，地势北高南低。宫城整体平面呈长方形，方向北偏西8度，南北248.39米、东西172.11米，仅在南面正中设门，建筑遗迹破坏较为严重。较大的夯土基址有两处，一处位于宫城南门内，一处位于宫城中部，两处建筑基址与南门均在宫城的中轴线上。贞陵神道石刻群自南向北依次为：石柱1对、翼马1对、鸵鸟1对（现存东侧1件）、仗马及牵马人各5对（原应各10件，现存仗马6件，新发现牵马人2件）、石人10对（原应20件，地表现存11件，新发现4件）。在南门阙以南的蕃酋殿建筑遗址出土蕃酋石人像6件。贞陵北门石刻除石狮1对，应有3对仗马及牵马人，地表现存仗马4件，新发现牵马人1件。相比较乾陵的石刻群而言，其石刻群雕凿较为粗糙。
projects.content_en: The Tang dynasty, from Emperor Gaozu Li Yuan's ascension in 618 AD to Emperor Ai Li Zhu's abdication in 907 AD, lasted 289 years through 21 emperors including Gaozu, Taizong, Gaozong, and Xuanzong. Because Wu Zetian was buried together with Emperor Gaozong, there are a total of 20 Tang imperial mausoleums. Except for the two mausoleums of Emperor Zhaozong (Heling) and Emperor Ai (Wenling), the remaining 18 are all located in the Guanzhong area of Shaanxi, stretching from Pucheng, Fuping, Sanyuan, Jingyang, and Liquan in the east to Qianxian in the west, spanning 150 km east-west, known as the 'Eighteen Mausoleums of Guanzhong.' The basic form of Tang mausoleums can be divided into two types: one is the inverted-bowl-shaped earthen mound built on high plateaus, including the Xian, Zhuang, and Duan mausoleums built on the Jingyuan and Xumuyuan plateaus of Sanyuan County, and the Jing mausoleum built on the northern plateau of Qianxian County, all located at altitudes above 500 to 800 m, with high plateaus and thick earth, convenient for deep burial. The other type uses the natural mountain terrain of the island-like hills north of the Wei River, chiseling tomb chambers into the southern slope of the mountain to form mausoleums, at altitudes of about 1,200 to 1,600 m; because of their vast scope and magnificent appearance, they are called 'mountain mausoleums,' and the remaining 14 Tang mausoleums all belong to this category. For example, Zhaoling faces steep cliffs to the south, so it follows the mountain and rocks, building beam bridges as plank roads to reach the tomb gate. Other mausoleums completely chisel stepped tomb passages from the foot of the mountain to reach the tomb gate. After burial, there is no trace at all, 'so that after a change of dynasty, its location would not be known,' and this was established as a system, followed by generations. The development and evolution of the Tang mausoleum park form can be roughly divided into four stages: The first stage is the early Tang Zhaoling and Xianling, belonging to the exploratory stage of borrowing from the Han and Wei imperial mausoleum systems. At that time, the mausoleum park layout was not yet standardized, so the forms were completely different, but their designs had a profound influence on later ones. For example, Zhaoling pioneered the 'using the mountain as the mausoleum' style; the Six Steeds of Zhaoling and the stone statues of 14 foreign tribal chiefs became precedents for placing foreign chief stone statues and north gate stone horses in all later Tang mausoleum parks. The square mausoleum park of Xianling, the stone pillars of the spirit path, and the companion tombs distributed on the east side of the mausoleum park were also adopted by later imperial mausoleums. The second stage is the prosperous Tang Qianling, Dingling, and Qiaoling, marking the formal formation of the Tang imperial mausoleum park system. The mausoleum park plane layout was designed as square as possible, with local adjustments according to terrain. The spirit path sets three gate towers to the south; the lower palace is arranged on the west side of the spirit path between the Rutai gate tower and the Quetai gate tower; companion tombs are distributed on the east side of the spirit path. The mausoleum park stone carving combination basically formed a standard, with a sharp increase in types and quantities, tall forms, and orderly arrangement. Inheriting the characteristic of large stone carving volume from the first stage, the south gate lions are generally 2.7 to 3 m high, and stone figures are usually about 4 m high. The third stage basically followed the prosperous Tang mausoleum park layout, such as the Tailing-Qianling model, while also producing some new adjustments and changes. Starting from Tailing, the plane of mountain-based mausoleum parks no longer pursued a square layout, but flexibly adjusted according to terrain, often呈 irregular shapes. The stone figures on both sides of the spirit path are divided into civil officials on the left and military officials on the right; the stone carving individuals became smaller, such as the lions outside the gate being 1.5 to 1.7 m high, and stone figures usually 2.5 to 2.9 m high. The lower palace scale decreased, and the number of companion tombs decreased. The fourth stage saw the decline of the Tang imperial mausoleum system. Except for Zhenling, the mausoleum park scale gradually became smaller, and the gate towers no longer used the triple-gate-tower form. The stone carving combination was basically stable, with the stone carving volume becoming even smaller; by the time of Jingling, the stone lion height was less than 1 m, and the stone figure height was less than 2 m, and the companion burial system gradually disappeared. Emperor Taizong's Zhaoling is located at the main peak of Jiuzong Mountain, 22 km northeast of Liquan County town, Xianyang City. The mausoleum construction began in the 10th year of Zhenguan (636 AD) and was basically completed in the 23rd year of Zhenguan (649 AD), lasting 13 years. It was designated as one of the first batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1961. Zhaoling pioneered the imperial 'using the mountain as the mausoleum' system. The 'Tang Huiyao' records: Emperor Taizong said to his attendants: 'In ancient times, the mountain was used as a tomb; this is indeed convenient. I see Jiuzong Mountain standing alone and winding around, so by chiseling alongside it, a mountain mausoleum can be placed there.' The main peak of Jiuzong Mountain has a precipitous terrain, at an altitude of 1,888 m, with rolling hills on both east and west sides, the Jing River winding behind it, and the Wei River winding in front, making it even more imposing. 'Since it uses the mountain terrain, although no mound is raised, it is naturally high and open.' Historical records state that Zhaoling chiseled stone into the mountain to form the underground palace (tomb chamber), with the passage (tomb passage) to the tomb chamber 75 zhang deep, with five stone gates set front and back. To allow palace attendants to make offerings as usual, houses were also built on the mountain. And because the mountain terrain was steep and travel was inconvenient, beam bridges were built as plank roads following the mountain and rocks, hanging over a hundred ren (ancient unit), winding 230 steps around the mountain to reach the underground palace gate. The Zhaoling mausoleum park is the largest among all Tang dynasty imperial mausoleum parks, 12.65 km long north-south and 15.45 km long east-west, spanning 4 townships (Zhaoling, Yanxia, Zhaozhen, Beitun), with an area of 113.15 square kilometers, accounting for about one-fifth of the entire Liquan County. The mausoleum park has inner and outer two cities; the inner city is square, with walls built on all four sides and a city gate opened on each side. On the north side of the inner city are the altar and Xuanwu Gate; inside the gate, 14 stone statues of minority ethnic group leaders of the time are arranged, of which only 4 remain now; east and west chambers are set inside the gate, and the Six Steeds of Zhaoling stone carvings are relics in the east and west chambers. Currently, three main building complex sites remain: one is the South Spirit Gate and Xiandian (offering hall) site slightly east of the south side of Jiuzong Mountain, one is the Qindian (sleeping palace) site on the southwest side, and one is the North Sima Gate site on the north side. In addition, there are cave and stone chamber remains on the south and east sides of the mountainside. The North Sima Gate is a complete north-south axisymmetric building complex, 86 m long north-south and 61 m at its widest east-west, distributed on three small platforms on the northern ridge of Jiuzong Mountain; the entire site terrain is high in the south and low in the north, with gullies on both east and west sides. The building remains gradually rise from south to north, sequentially including: on the first platform, a pair of triple-gate-tower foundations,推测 corridor sites for halberd displays, and 4 small buildings outside the north wall; on the north edge of the second platform, a hip-and-gable style gate site, north wall, and brick drainage ditch; above the second platform, only west-side building remains survive, sequentially from south to north including side halls, square small buildings, and stepped long corridors. Outside the building complex, there are rammed-earth walls with brick-paved drainage aprons, and only the west side retains部分 wall foundations. At the northernmost end of the building complex are east and west double gate towers, 31.5 m apart, with only the lower part of the gate tower platforms remaining, of the same form, with rammed-earth platform foundations inside and brick walls outside. The bottom of the gate towers is surrounded by brick-paved drainage aprons 85 cm wide, corresponding to the gate tower body in a triple shape. The south and east slopes of Jiuzong Mountain and the plain area at the foot of the mountain are the Zhaoling companion tomb area, with a total of 198 companion tombs according to statistics. The number, scale, and form of its companion tombs are the greatest among all Tang imperial mausoleums, reflecting the majestic momentum and strictly hierarchical social system of the rising period of the feudal dynasty. Companion tombs include those with tomb chambers chiseled into the mountain, those with mounds in inverted-bowl or conical shapes to resemble mountain forms, and those with neither mound nor tree; in front of the tombs, there are often stone figures, stone sheep, stone tigers, and stone steles. These tombs are generally arranged naturally from north to south according to chronological order, while the tomb height is limited according to official rank. Qianling is the joint burial mausoleum of Emperor Gaozong of Tang and Wu Zetian, located at Liangshan Mountain, 6 km northwest of Qianxian County town, Xianyang City. Qianling construction began after Emperor Gaozong's death. In the 1st year of Hongdao (683 AD), Emperor Gaozong died in Luoyang; in the 1st year of Wenming (684 AD), he was buried in Qianling; in the 1st year of Shenlong (705 AD), Wu Zetian died in Luoyang; in the 2nd year of Shenlong (706 AD), she was jointly buried in Qianling. It was designated as one of the first batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 1961. Qianling has an excellent site. Liangshan Mountain is 80 km east of Chang'an, with Jiuzong to its east, the Wu River winding to its west, hills connected to the north, and plains to the south, with a solitary peak rising sharply, tall and graceful, making it an ideal place for building a mausoleum. Because Liangshan Mountain is located in the Qian (northwest) position relative to Chang'an, the mausoleum was named Qianling. The Qianling mausoleum park has a rigorous layout. At Zhangjiabao, 1.5 km northwest of Qianxian County town, there are two 8-m-high earthen mounds, which are the remains of the first gate passage of Qianling; 3 km north are the South Two Peaks; from the two peaks northward is the spirit path, with stone carvings on both sides including a pair of stone huabiao (ornamental columns, which in ancient times symbolized the emperor's willingness to receive remonstrance), a pair of flying horses, a pair of vermilion birds, five pairs of stone horses (including three pairs of horse handlers), and ten pairs of stone figures holding swords with both hands; 13.5 m north of the stone figures are the Shushengji Stele (in the west) and the Wordless Stele (in the east); behind them are 61 stone figures, which are statues of foreign tribal chief envoys who attended the funeral; the Vermilion Bird Gate is at the southern foot of Liangshan Mountain, with a pair of stone lions in front of the gate, and north of the stone lions is the site of the Xiandian (offering hall). The stone carving group system of Qianling had some influence on other later imperial mausoleums; for example, Emperor Suzong's Jianling and Emperor Ruizong's Qiaoling both followed the Qianling system. The Qianling mausoleum park is built using natural mountain peaks. The north peak of Liangshan Mountain is where the Qianling underground palace is located. Tall city walls built around the north peak are called the palace city, with a gate opened on each side, and stone carvings and gate towers set outside the gates. Outside the Vermilion Bird Gate, a broad spirit path is built using the low-lying area, with its southern end reaching directly to the foot of the Milk Peaks. Between the two Milk Peaks, a natural gateway to the mausoleum park is formed, with gate towers built on top of the Milk Peaks. Together with the stone carving artworks such as huabiao, winged horses, vermilion birds, and stone figures on both sides of the spirit path, they jointly create the pre-mausoleum architectural environment, forming a strong spatial contrast with the natural mountain peak above the underground palace—the North Peak. The tomb passage and tomb gate are located at the middle waist of the southern slope of the mountain, chiseled into the natural limestone mountain. The tomb passage is a north-south slope, with a total length of about 65 m and an east-west width of 3.87 m. Qianling originally had inner and outer double cities, and the inner city wall foundation remains still exist. Its south city wall foundation is 1,438 m long; 657 m from east to west, there is a rammed-earth mound remnant 1 m above ground and 10 m in diameter, which is the site of the Vermilion Bird Gate. The south city wall has water drainage culverts built where it crosses the Huangchao Gully, constructed with stone strips. The north city wall foundation is 1,450 m long, the east city wall foundation is 1,582 m long, and the west city wall foundation is 1,450 m long; the city wall foundation rammed earth is 2.1 to 2.5 m wide. City corner remains: the southeast city corner is 7.5 m high, the northeast city corner is 5.1 m high, the northwest city corner is 5.5 m high, and the southwest city corner is 10 m high, all built of rammed earth. The northwest and northeast city corners have stone strip-built foundations. Within the Qianling mausoleum area, 17 companion tombs are distributed. Among them, Crown Prince Yide Li Chongrun's tomb was designated as a 'mausoleum' (hao mu wei ling), making it one of the largest and highest-ranking Tang imperial mausoleum companion tombs ever excavated. Princess Yongtai Li Xianhui's tomb was also designated as a 'mausoleum,' making her the only one among 212 Tang princesses to receive this规格 treatment, and also the earliest excavated and relatively high-ranking Tang female imperial tomb. When Crown Prince Zhanghuai Li Xian was reburied, he was accompanied with the rites of Prince Yong, the lowest rank. Emperor Xuanzong's Tailing is located at Jinsu Mountain, 15 km northeast of Pucheng County town. It was designated as the fifth batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 2001. Jinsu Mountain is 4.2 km east-west and 2 km north-south, divided into two larger peaks, east and west. The Tailing mausoleum park surrounds the west peak, 1.2 km east-west and 1.3 km north-south, with a roughly square plane; the tomb chamber is located on the north-south gate axis, and the east and west gates are respectively set on the ridges extending left and right from the top of the west peak. Tailing uses the mountain as the mausoleum, chiseling the tomb chamber into the mountain belly, and building mausoleum walls around the foot of the mountain, divided into inner and outer cities. The inner city wall originally had four gates on all four sides; limited by terrain, the four gate sites were chosen according to local conditions, not in a symmetrical layout. Except for the south gate located on the gentle slope in front of the mountain, the east, west, and north gates are all built on ridges or hillside platforms, with narrow areas. The straight-line distance between the east and west gates is 1,168.8 m, and between the south and north gates is 1,133.8 m. Each of the four corners of the city wall has a corner gate tower, with great disparities in distances between corner gate towers; for example, the straight-line distance from the southwest corner gate tower to the southeast corner gate tower is 1,176.9 m, while the straight-line distance from the northwest corner gate tower to the northeast corner gate tower is only 765.3 m. Affected by terrain, the city wall plane is roughly an irregular pentagon. Except for the south wall being relatively straight, the other three walls are not straight extensions. The north wall starts from the northwest corner gate tower, bends northeast to connect with the north gate, then connects with the closer northeast corner gate tower; the west wall is built on the slope on the west side of the mountain ridge, roughly arc-shaped; the east wall basically winds and undulates along the ridge direction, in a snake-like shape. Tailing's above-ground buildings include the Xiandian (offering hall), lower palace, and mausoleum office, which no longer exist today. Its companion tomb, according to records in 'Tang Huiyao,' 'Chang'an Zhi,' 'Wenxian Tongkao,' and 'Guanzhong Lingmu Zhi,' is only one, namely the already excavated Gao Lishi tomb. Tailing's stone carvings are relatively well preserved in quantity, but in poor condition. Tailing's stone carvings (excluding foreign chief statues) should originally have 50 pieces (groups) (war horses, bases, and horse handlers counted as one group), with 41 pieces (groups) currently existing on the ground. 9 pieces (groups) of stone carvings were newly cleaned and unearthed, including the fourth war horse base on the west side of the south gate spirit path, 4 fragments of foreign chief statues, 1 foreign chief statue base, the third war horse on the east side of the north gate spirit path (including war horse and base, horse handler) and the first war horse on the west side (including war horse and base), and a stone tiger and a stone figure blank were also unearthed at the north gate. Emperor Xuanzong's Zhenling is located at Beizhong Mountain, north of Cuihuang Village, Baiwang Township, Jingyang County. It was designated as the fifth batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in 2001. The Zhenling mausoleum park spans Jingyang and Chunhua counties north-south. The terrain within the park is complex, with steep mountains; on the surface, only the Quetai (magpie platform) sites, corner gate tower sites, earthen gate towers in front of each gate, and above-ground stone carvings remain. The mausoleum park city wall surrounds Beizhong Mountain, built according to the natural mountain terrain. Its layout is an irregular shape narrow in the south and wide in the north; except for the south gate located at the relatively gentle southern foot of Beizhong Mountain, the other three gates are all built on ridges. The city foundation is rammed; the south wall is located in the relatively gentle area at the foot of the mountain, extending in a straight line; the west wall winds northward from the southwest corner gate tower along the ridge to the west gate, then connects northwestward along the ridge to the northwest corner gate tower; the east wall has a gentler slope northward from the southeast corner gate tower, taking a straight line to the east gate, and north of the east gate winds along the ridge to the northeast corner gate tower; the north wall has the most complex terrain, with the western part明显 extending toward the southwest ridge, and connections to both the northeast and northwest corner gate towers requiring passing through steep slopes and gullies, with large undulations. The Zhenling lower palace site is located on the platform north of Miaobeihou Village, Baiwang Town, Jingyang County, 299.24 m southeast of the west Quetai site, with terrain high in the north and low in the south. The palace city overall plane is rectangular, oriented 8 degrees west of north, 248.39 m north-south and 172.11 m east-west, with a gate only in the center of the south side; the building remains are relatively severely damaged. There are two larger rammed-earth foundation sites, one inside the south gate of the palace city and one in the center of the palace city; both building foundation sites and the south gate are on the central axis of the palace city. The Zhenling spirit path stone carving group from south to north依次 includes: 1 pair of stone pillars, 1 pair of winged horses, 1 pair of ostriches (only the east piece现存), 5 pairs each of war horses and horse handlers (originally 10 each, currently 6 war horses existing, 2 horse handlers newly discovered), and 10 pairs of stone figures (originally 20, currently 11 existing on the ground, 4 newly discovered). At the foreign chief hall building site south of the south gate tower, 6 foreign chief stone figure statues were unearthed. The Zhenling north gate stone carvings, besides 1 pair of stone lions, should have 3 pairs of war horses and horse handlers, with 4 war horses currently existing on the ground and 1 horse handler newly discovered. Compared with the Qianling stone carving group, its stone carving group is relatively roughly carved.
